aliases: Collegiate Church of Saint Peter at Westminster

claims.text: Westminster Abbey is a large Anglican church that is formally known as the Collegiate Church of Saint Peter at Westminster.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The abbey has been the prestigious location for the coronations of 40 different English and British monarchs since the year 1066.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The church has also hosted at least 16 royal weddings, including the marriage of Prince William and Catherine Middleton in 2011.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The origins of the church date back to around the year 959, when it was established by a community of Benedictine monks on what was then known as Thorney Island.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Construction of the present magnificent Gothic church began much later, in the year 1245, under the orders of King Henry III.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Unusually for an English church, the abbey's architecture was heavily inspired by French Gothic styles, featuring the highest nave of any Gothic church in England.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The western towers were not added until the 18th century, designed by Nicholas Hawksmoor to blend the abbey's Gothic style with contemporary Baroque elements.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The famous Henry VII Chapel, located at the east end of the church, is widely considered a masterpiece of Perpendicular Gothic architecture.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The abbey is the final resting place for more than 3,300 people, including 18 British monarchs, famous scientists, and prominent poets.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: In 1987, the abbey was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site due to its immense historic and symbolic significance.
claims.subject: self
